diagnosis: Customer upgraded from a lower plan to Business mid-cycle on the 14th. Invoice INV-88213 likely includes a prorated credit for the old plan and a prorated charge for the new plan, causing the total to differ from the standalone plan price. This matches the explanation in KB-0001.
reply: Thank you for your question. The higher amount on your first invoice after upgrading to Business is due to mid-cycle proration. When you upgraded on the 14th, we credited the unused portion of your previous plan and then charged the prorated cost of the Business plan for the rest of the billing period. That's why the total differs from the standard plan price. For details, please refer to our knowledge base article "Understanding mid-cycle proration on plan upgrades." If you have further concerns about invoice line items, feel free to provide the specific line and the amount you expected, and we can investigate (see KB-0009).
